headline: Energy shock weighs on stocks while AI earnings test resolve
body: Friday's close capped a jittery week: the Dow fell 1.23% (-652.82 points) to 52,215.16, the S&P 500 slipped 0.52% to 7,623.68, and the Nasdaq eased 0.21% to 25,955.34, even as energy shares rallied on crude's push toward $100 a barrel amid the prolonged US-Iran standoff, with Iran keeping the Strait of Hormuz closed and Washington maintaining a counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Consumer and healthcare names bore the brunt of the pullback, while chipmakers and other tech stocks steadied after Thursday's AI-spending-driven selloff, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index edging higher and names like CrowdStrike posting standout gains. The split tape - commodity-driven weakness layered on lingering AI-valuation nerves - reads as investors treating the energy shock as a headline risk to monitor rather than a reason to broadly de-risk, for now.

Positioning data reflects that same unease: the latest AAII survey (mid-October) shows bearish sentiment at 41.6%, now outnumbering bulls at 38.7% and running above its historical average for a 36th straight week, while neutral readings stay unusually thin. That points to a market that's cautious rather than complacent heading into the year's heaviest earnings stretch, with Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon all due to report in the coming days against a backdrop where roughly 84% of S&P 500 reporters so far have beaten estimates. A scan of retail forums didn't surface a dominant single-stock narrative or meme-style spike today, so this read leans more on index action, oil, and earnings positioning than on social-media sentiment.
